title: 新潟県知事選　「県民に信を問う」原発再稼働めぐる花角知事の発言が争点に　5月14日告示・31日投開票
extracted_text: 告示まで2週間を切った新潟県知事選挙。争点の一つとなるのが柏崎刈羽原発の再稼働をめぐる花角知事の発言です。8年前の知事選から繰り返してきた「県民に信を問う」という言葉が議論を呼んでいます。 【柏崎刈羽原発　稲垣武之 所長】「大きな事故を福島第一原発で起こした当事者。その反省と教訓は決して忘れることなく、今後、安全最優先で運転を続けていく」 【花角知事】「しっかり熟慮して一定の決断を下し、県民に職を賭して信を問う。安全性がしっかりと検証されて、かつ県民の納得がない限り動かしません」 現職の花角知事は8年前の知事選初挑戦のときから、原発の再稼働については自身で判断を下し「県民に信を問う」と繰り返してきました。ただ、その方法をめぐっては… 【花角知事】「『信を問う』という言葉は想像できるものがありますよね。何度も申し上げている『信』という言葉を使えば信任・不信任ですよ。存在を賭けるということ」 【花角知事】「そろそろ結論を出さなければいけないという中で県議会に信任・不信任をお諮りする方向が適切だと判断した」 県が実施した意識調査では県民の6割が再稼働の条件は整っていないと回答する中、再稼働容認の立場の自民党が単独過半数を占める県議会で「信を問う」とした花角知事。 【土田竜吾 県議】「現状に対して、ある意味議論を打ち切って再稼働の理解に了解するというのは、この理由を出すというのは、私は不適切だと思うんですけれども」 【花角知事】「行政の姿勢としてここまで材料がそろい、判断が行われたのであれば、ここは速やかに事態を動かしていかざるをえないというふうに思っています」 【土田竜吾 県議】「もう政治判断だということだと思いますので、県民に信を問うというところの原点に立ち返ってもらって、しっかりと責任を果たしていただくことを強く要望する」 しかし、県民が住民投票や選挙などで直接意思を表明する場は設けられず、花角知事を信任する付帯決議案が賛成多数で可決され、国に再稼動の了承が伝えられました。 【土田竜吾 県議】「県民に信を問うと言いながら、県議会に信任・不信任をうかがうという形で進められてしまった。これはやはり約束違反じゃないですかと。これからの県政、しっかりと約束を守る、県政皆さんの不安に寄り添う県政に転換していかなければいけない」 【土田竜吾 県議】「雪のときの避難の課題だったり、東京電力が運転することへの適格性の不安だったり、様々な不安な思いをお持ちの方が県内にたくさんいらっしゃるというのが現状」 自身は原発に対する県民の不安に寄り添う県政を行っていくと主張。避難道路の整備など安全対策に力を入れ、さらに東京電力へのチェック体制も強化すると話します。その一方で… 【土田竜吾 県議】「いま動いているものに対して停止をする権限というのが、新潟県が持っているという状況ではなかなかないというところでもあるので」 【安中聡 氏】「この原発への反対、原発の廃止、そして県民投票条例の制定。これを県民の皆さんに訴えていきたいというふうに考えている」 福島第一原発事故の収束は見通せず、国際情勢も不安定さを増す中、いつ起こるかわからない地震の不安におびえながら原発を動かすのは危険だと指摘します。 【安中聡 氏】「私が当選するということは、原発廃止を願う方が出て、それで当選するという話になるから、県民の声を十分に聞いているということになる。前の知事の決断というのは間違っていたのだから、それは今回動かしている柏崎刈羽原発というのは止めていただきたいというのを率直にお話しさせていただく」 【安中聡 氏】「県民の声をちゃんと聞かなきゃだめなんだというような土壌づくり。これも並行してやらなくてはいけない」 来県した赤沢経産大臣に原子力発電に関する県民の理解促進の国の取り組みを改めて要望。ただ、ほかの候補予定者が原発の再稼動プロセスを争点化したいのに対し… 【花角知事】「私がやってきたこと、取り組んできたこと、その全てを評価していただきたい。これを一貫して申し上げている」
translated_text: The Niigata Prefecture governor election is now less than two weeks away from the announcement. One of the key issues is Governor Hanakumi's remarks regarding the restart of the Kashiwazaki-Kariwa Nuclear Power Plant. The phrase "asking the people for their trust" that has been repeated since the governor's election 8 years ago is generating discussion. [Kashiwazaki-Kariwa Nuclear Power Plant, Manager Takeyuki Inagaki] "We were the party responsible for the major accident at Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Plant. Those reflections and lessons must never be forgotten, and we will continue operating with safety as the top priority going forward." [Governor Hanakumi] "I have carefully considered and made a certain decision, staking my position on the line and asking for the people's trust. I will not proceed unless safety has been thoroughly verified and the public is convinced." The incumbent Governor Hanakumi has repeatedly said "asking the people for their trust" regarding nuclear plant restart since first running for governor 8 years ago, pledging to make the decision personally. However, regarding the method... [Governor Hanakumi] "The phrase 'asking for trust' is something you can imagine, right? By using the word 'trust' that I have said many times, it means approval or disapproval. It's about staking one's existence." [Governor Hanakumi] "Among the need to reach a conclusion soon, I judged it appropriate to seek approval or disapproval from the prefectural assembly." While a prefectural survey showed 60% of residents answered that conditions for restart are not met, Governor Hanakumi, who takes a pro-restart stance, has said he will "ask the people for their trust" in the prefectural assembly where the LDP holds a single majority. [Prefectural Assembly Member Ryugo Tsuchida] "To cut off debate on the current situation and seek understanding for restart based on this reason—I think that is inappropriate." [Governor Hanakumi] "As an administrative stance, since materials have been gathered and a judgment made, I believe we must move forward promptly." [Prefectural Assembly Member Ryugo Tsuchida] "I think this is ultimately a political judgment, so I strongly urge you to return to the original point of 'asking the people for their trust' and fulfill your responsibilities." However, no mechanism was provided for residents to directly express their will through referendums or elections, and a supplementary resolution approving of Governor Hanakumi was passed by majority vote, conveying to the national government the approval for restart. [Prefectural Assembly Member Ryugo Tsuchida] "While saying he would 'ask the people for their trust,' it was carried out by seeking approval or disapproval from the prefectural assembly instead. This is truly a breach of promise, isn't it? From now on, the prefectural government must change to one that firmly keeps its promises and addresses the anxieties of everyone." [Prefectural Assembly Member Ryugo Tsuchida] "The current situation is that many people within the prefecture have various anxieties—whether it's evacuation challenges during snow, or concerns about the suitability of Tokyo Electric Power Company operating the plant." He advocates for a prefectural government that addresses the anxieties of residents regarding nuclear plants. He plans to focus on safety measures such as preparing evacuation roads, and also strengthening the verification system for Tokyo Electric Power Company. On the other hand... [Prefectural Assembly Member Ryugo Tsuchida] "Under the current situation where Niigata Prefecture does not have the authority to stop something that is already operating, it's difficult to do so." [Mr. Satoshi Annaka] "I want to appeal to the residents of this prefecture about opposing this nuclear plant, its abolition, and establishing a referendum ordinance." He points out that operating the nuclear plant while anxious about earthquakes that could occur at any time is dangerous, given that there's no end in sight to the Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Plant accident and the international situation is increasingly unstable. [Mr. Satoshi Annaka] "If I am elected, it means those wishing for nuclear abolition will have come forward and won through my election, which means the voices of the residents are being fully heard. The former governor's decision was wrong, so I would like to frankly state that we want the Kashiwazaki-Kariwa Nuclear Power Plant, which is currently operating, to be stopped this time." [Mr. Satoshi Annaka] "We must also work in parallel on building the groundwork to properly listen to the residents' voices." They renewed their request to Minister of Economy, Trade and Industry Akazawa, who visited the prefecture, for the national government's efforts to promote understanding among residents regarding nuclear power generation. However, while other candidates plan to make the nuclear plant restart process an election issue... [Governor Hanakumi] "I want all of what I have done and worked on to be evaluated. This is what I have consistently said."
title_en: Niigata Governor Election: Governor Hanakumi's Remarks on Nuclear Plant Restart Become Key Issue — 'Asking the People for Their Trust' — Announcement May 14, Vote Counting May 31
